title: Vue tests: behavior, timing, and contracts
outcome: Write component tests for failed saves, async races, and accessible interaction.
useCase: Changes to complex forms and route-driven panes.
drawbacks: Mocks and simulated DOM tests have limits.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Test the promise the user sees.

trace.title: Arrange a boundary
trace.detail: A pure test checks a transformation. A component test mounts a small UI and exercises its public behavior. A browser test verifies real navigation, layout, and browser APIs. Choose the layer that can observe the defect.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Arrange the state and fake boundary → act as a user → flush the required update boundary → assert visible outcome and emitted contract. Confirm the test fails when the repair is removed.

For focus trapping, hydration, scroll, and browser back behavior, run a real browser check. A simulated DOM does not implement all browser layout/accessibility behavior.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Testing private implementation details makes refactors expensive. Broad snapshots may miss the important failure. Arbitrary sleeps make the test depend on machine speed.
